`output_pm = DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM` while `switch_on` (self-powered: `armed` 1, `live` 1, `served_pm` 1000, so D.1 reduces to `base_pm`); the console subject at distance `d_c ≤ DOCK_STATUS_CONSOLE_MAX_PX` from the glow origin is lit iff `c(d_c) = ⌊ DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM × F(d_c, R) / 1000 ⌋ ≥ LIT_ON_PM`, `R = DOCK_STATUS_REACH_PX`, `F(d, R) = ⌊1000 × (R − d) / R⌋`

== E416
**Constraints.** (C1) `R ≥ REACH_MIN_PX` 24 (I-REACH). (C2) the console is lit with margin at the farthest allowed placement: `c(DOCK_STATUS_CONSOLE_MAX_PX) ≥ LIT_ON_PM` plus a margin that absorbs a placement tolerance. (C3) the glow is small and dim: its `section_emission` term `⌊ output_pm × R / 1000 ⌋` is at most one sixth of an ordinary fixture's 144 (1000 × 144 / 1000), that is **at most 24**, so it reads as a status light and not as a lamp that lights the room. **C3 is enforced by I-DOCK** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the ruled ranges (`DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM` 300–800, `DOCK_STATUS_REACH_PX` up to 96) allow up to ⌊800 × 96 / 1000⌋ = 76, so a range check alone left C3 unenforced. (C4) the glow is a FIXTURE under the 28-fixture cap (I-CAPS (a)), so it needs no new cap: the largest loaded set is 21 fixtures (registry `mvp_fixture_counts`), leaving 7 for dock glows.

content.content:
**CT-10. The console seam: the only simulation write.**
*Rule.* The chart submits nothing. The **pod console press** (Interaction's CONSOLE subject, `tool_required` NONE) is the only simulation write and the only commitment (WM:1225, WM:1301): no "confirm sortie", no resume-and-hop gesture, no confirmation dialog anywhere on this layer. Resolution at the press, in the Input Adapter's seam:
1. **From a derelict:** HOME is implied (WM-4, WM-8: "from a derelict the press carries HOME implicitly"). If the chart is opened there it shows the bracket on HOME as the only focusable node, and the planned-sortie line from the pod's node to HOME is drawn from `pod_at` (not from `ChartPick`), because that is the only legal move; the selection cannot move to another node. This implied line carries the same single meaning as CT-7's dashed line (the endpoint of the pick, or of the leg in flight) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: while `transit_state == IDLE` it is the target the next console press carries; the in-flight OUT-leg route is CT-15's; it is not a recommendation.
2. **From HOME with a valid pick:** the press submits `pod_hop{target_id := ChartPick}` at the POD prompt, or `berth{derelict_id := ChartPick}` at the DOCK prompt (WM-21). Which of the two a press means is decided by **which prompt was pressed** (the verb-resolution table below), never by a mode of the chart.
3. **From HOME with no valid pick, at a prompt that needs a pick (`pod_hop`, `berth`):** the press **opens the chart** (host-local, no refusal, no simulation effect), **even when exactly one legal target exists**: an auto-implied hop from HOME would make the press both choice and commitment. Default focus on opening is the pod's own node (HOME), never a target, so focus is never a recommendation. In SOLO the open requests a pause as in CT-4 and is a governed raise (CT-3). **This rule applies only to `pod_hop` and `berth`; `unberth` takes no payload, never needs a pick and is never swallowed by it** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
4. **Verb-resolution table** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; keyed on the facts the Adapter can read at the press: `pod_at`, `transit_state`, whether a record is `berthed`, and `ChartPick`; the prompt is the Interaction subject that was pressed)*. Console preconditions that are Interaction's and Web Map's (in reach, lit, `console_ready`) are evaluated first and answered in words on the register plate; the table starts after them.

| Row | `pod_at` | `transit_state` | `berthed` record | `ChartPick` | Prompt pressed | Result of the press |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | a derelict | IDLE | n/a (berth starts only from HOME) | not read | POD | `pod_hop{target_id := HOME_ID}` (HOME is implied, WM-4, WM-8) |
| R1b *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | a derelict | IDLE | n/a | not read | DOCK | **no DOCK prompt exists there** (WM-21: `berth` starts only from HOME; the DOCK subject is anchored on the home dock room, ASK-CT-13); if Interaction exposes it anyway, the press submits no command, opens no chart and Web Map answers `NOT_DOCKED_HERE` in words |
| R2 | HOME | IDLE | none | valid | POD | `pod_hop{target_id := ChartPick}` |
| R3 | HOME | IDLE | none | NONE or invalid | POD | opens the chart (entry origin `CONSOLE`, TX-18); no command |
| R4a | HOME | IDLE | none | valid | DOCK | `berth{derelict_id := ChartPick}` |
| R4b | HOME | IDLE | none | NONE or invalid | DOCK | opens the chart (as R3) |
| R5 | HOME | IDLE | a record B | **not read** | DOCK | `unberth{}` (no payload; the DOCK prompt's verb is `unberth` while a record is berthed; never opens the chart) |
| R6 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | HOME | IDLE | a record B (not ABSORBED) | not read (`legal_targets` is `{}`, so a pick is always invalid) | POD | **no chart opens and no `pod_hop{target}` is built from the pick**; the press is routed to Web Map so the register plate shows its `BERTH_PENDING` words (ASK-CT-13: Web Map answers a payload-less `pod_hop` while a record is berthed with `BERTH_PENDING`); the layer renders no words |
| R7 | any | LEG, ARRIVING, BERTHING | any | not read | either | no command and no chart: the refusal words are Web Map's (`IN_TRANSIT`, `BUSY`), shown on the register plate |
| R8 | `IN_FLIGHT` | any | any | not read | none exists | no console can be pressed |

The POD prompt and the DOCK prompt are **two Interaction subjects (or two prompts) on the dock room's console**, because pod at HOME, nothing berthed and a valid pick leave both `pod_hop{pick}` and `berth{pick}` legal, and one `interact` cannot mean both. If the neighbours keep a single CONSOLE subject the berth path has no unambiguous trigger, so this split is a **blocking requirement for the console story** (ASK-CT-13 to Interaction, Web Map & Transit and the Layout `subject_anchors`; the table is this GDD's proposal and the neighbours' agreement is recorded in Open Questions, not assumed). The prompt wording stays state-neutral (IA-40) and never names a target, distance or cost.
5. **Stale-pick echo (GATE ITEM before `/create-stories`, owned by Interaction, ASK-CT-14)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Because the pick is invisible at the console and the hop has no confirm, the POD and DOCK plates carry a small text-free echo of the pick (**at R1, from a derelict, the echo is HOME's node glyph**, so the player sees what the irreversible press carries; at R2 and R4a it is the pick's): the pick's node glyph as the chart draws it (the plain rectangle, the Foundry silhouette and, if seen, the tick), nothing else; no name, no ordinal, no distance, no cost (G6 and the CT-44 exception are unchanged). A clear-after-N-seconds timer is rejected (a timeout would change what a press means without the player acting). A playtest observable records presses made with a stale pick (CT-GF-12). Re-opening the chart with focus on the existing pick was considered and **not adopted** (default focus stays HOME; the UX spec may revisit it).
The seam (the Adapter injects the host-local pick into the payload at R2 and R4a; a no-pick press at R3 and R4b routes to "open chart") is **accepted** by the Controller (PCI:100 and Interactions row 17) and by Interaction (IA-40) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: "provisional" and "degraded if refused" retired; ASK-CT-1 is answered; ASK-CT-13 and ASK-CT-14 are the new asks)*.
*Why.* P2 (the commitment at the console, not on a menu); WM-8; an irreversible, fuel-costing write that depends on a hidden host-local pick needs its resolution stated per fact. *Source.* WM-8, WM-21, WM-22, WM:1225, WM:1301; IA-40; PCI Interactions row 17. **-> ADR candidate (d):** the pick-to-console submit seam.

#### C. Drawing the web

=====
| ASK-CT-13 | Interaction, Web Map & Transit, Layout (`subject_anchors`) | **(new, BLOCKING for the console story; GATE ITEM before `/create-stories`)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* the pod console exposes **two subjects or prompts**, POD (`pod_hop`) and DOCK (`berth` / `unberth`), and Interaction adopts the verb-resolution table of CT-10 (R1 to R8): `unberth` needs no pick and never opens the chart; `pod_hop` and `berth` with no valid pick open the chart; the DOCK subject is anchored on the home dock room only (no DOCK prompt at a derelict, R1b); Web Map answers a payload-less `pod_hop` while a record is berthed with `BERTH_PENDING` and a DOCK press away from HOME with `NOT_DOCKED_HERE` (R6, R1b) | no unambiguous trigger for `berth` exists while one CONSOLE subject carries all three verbs and a valid pick makes both `pod_hop` and `berth` legal. **Stated fallback now** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: if Interaction keeps one CONSOLE subject, the single prompt resolves by state (a record berthed: `unberth`, R5; otherwise a valid pick: `pod_hop`, R2; no pick: opens the chart, R3) and `berth` has no MVP trigger, which removes the berth-and-weld loop (Moment 4) from MVP until a second console fixture exists; that is a scope cut the producer and creative-director must take, so the ask stays a gate |
| ASK-CT-14 | Interaction | **(new; GATE ITEM before `/create-stories`, raised from RECOMMENDED *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*)** a text-free echo of the pick's node glyph on the POD and DOCK plates (no name, ordinal, distance or cost), **and, at R1 (from a derelict), the echo of HOME's glyph** so the player sees what the irreversible press carries, and no timer that clears the pick. **Stated fallback now:** a commitment made on invisible host-local state is not deliberate (P2), so if Interaction declines the echo, `ChartPick` is cleared whenever a panel-opened chart (`entry_origin == PANEL`) closes to gameplay, and a console-opened chart (`entry_origin == CONSOLE`) keeps it, so a pick is only ever made and used inside one console visit; the cost is that picking from the panel becomes view-only, which the game-designer and UX spec must accept | a forgotten pick remains a plausible irreversible misfire; recorded by the playtest observable (CT-GF-12, AC-CT-124) |
| OQ-CT-36 | The verb-resolution table of CT-10 and the POD and DOCK split (ASK-CT-13) are this GDD's proposal; the agreement of Interaction, Web Map & Transit and Layout is not yet recorded. The console story is blocked on it; the only fallback is the scope cut stated in ASK-CT-13 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: ASK-CT-13, ASK-CT-14 and ASK-CT-15 are gate items before `/create-stories`)* | agent (Interaction, Web Map & Transit, Layout) | next GDD |

Since berth was already established as user-ruled, the Chart Table consumer's proposal becomes required rather than optional, which means Interaction needs to own the POD/DOCK split addition.

**IA-5 One contextual action: `select_verb`.** Given the focused object's classes and the tool in hand (Suit's `tool_in_hand`, Suit & Equipment, Designed — SE-40), the declaration row is chosen by: (1) the rows whose `tool_required` equals the tool in hand, lowest `priority` first; else (2) the bare-hand rows, lowest `priority` first; else (3) the lowest-`priority` row of the class, shown with its tool glyph and answered `NO_TOOL` on press. The choice is a function of (object classes, tool in hand, the `eligible` predicate) only — **never of hp, state, forced mode or served power** (IA-11). While the actor carries a module, the only selectable rows are `drop` placement and the declared carry-admitted rows (`admitted_while_carrying`: `install_module` on a HARDPOINT whose `compatible_defs(h)` lists the carried instance's def, and `pod_hop` on the pod CONSOLE; IA-28); any other world target while carrying is shown no prompt at all. *Example:* a scrubber with the welder in hand selects V1 `begin_patch`; with the cutter in hand it selects V8 `begin_cut`; with bare hands row (3) selects V1 and shows the welder glyph — the press answers `NO_TOOL`. *Alternatives considered:* hide the verb without the tool (the player never learns it exists); auto-equip the right tool (removes a Suit decision and makes `equip_tool` pointless). *Decides:* R11, HR-14 (one contextual action), D10.

296:**IA-33 Noise.** The declaration carries `noise_class` in {QUIET, TOOL, LOUD}. As channel owner, Interaction calls Attention's intake `push_stimulus(NOISE, source_ref, class)` once per *accrued* channel tick for TOOL-class verbs (cutter, welder, crank, scanner) and one-shot LOUD events at cut completion, seam-cut DONE (Assembly's `begin_seam_cut`, MSA-29), vent apply, throw landing and the `berth` apply (the pod console's `berth`, ruled LOUD; `unberth` and `pod_hop` stay QUIET) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)* *(Attention System, Designed — AT-3: the API and the class set {QUIET, TOOL, LOUD} confirmed)*. A tick that aborts before accrual pushes nothing. Units are Attention's; the Controller's `NOISE_PER_TICK` (walk, run, carry) is cited, never restated. A breaker close pushes nothing (the Graph's inrush is Attention's power stimulus through `power_use`); a door motor pushes nothing. Interaction states three relations Attention's units must satisfy, or the verbs become free or absurd: the TOOL-class per-tick unit lies between 2 and 6 so a 180-tick patch integrates to at least twice the walking noise of the same time and no more than 1.5 times the running noise; a LOUD one-shot is at least 30 ticks of the TOOL unit; and `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS ≤ 2 × TAU_ATT_TICKS` (IA-16) — Attention accepts all three (registry `noise_unit_relations` IR-1 to IR-3: `2 ≤ U_TOOL ≤ 6`, `U_LOUD ≥ 30 × U_TOOL`, `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS ≤ 2 × TAU_ATT_TICKS`). Attention never reads Audio (IDX:34). **Pillar 3 trace (ruled: it does not depend on sparks).** The Pillar 3 price of any channel is carried by two things that exist regardless of how Open Question 18 resolves: the target must be lit (IA-6, IA-7), so the job is done in light the web can see through Emitter State's exposure, and a dark job is impossible but for the three listed exceptions; and the tool's TOOL-class noise push on every accrued tick (above). Weld and cut sparks are non-emissive at MVP (art-director AD-6: no Light2D, not an Emitter State emitter), so the trace never rests on them.
